corrections.L3a: Old: `journalctl -o cat | grep -qi watchdog` under set -o pipefail; grep -q exits at the first match, journalctl gets SIGPIPE, rc 141 = FAIL on a real match (reproduced on the real journal: checks-test L3a OLD = 141). New: l3a_eval reads the whole journal; it requires 'Watchdog timeout' AND "Failed with result 'watchdog'" between the onset and the observed restart (+5 s); stale or unrelated lines fail.
corrections.L7c_and_recovery_waits: healthy_after EPOCH = verdict ok or rest, checked at/after the event; applied to L7c (both waits), L3a pass, L3b pass, L3b recovered. starting/unknown/hung/crashed/restart-loop/parse errors never count. The L7c window assertion (starting) is unchanged.
corrections.L4a_L4b: Per ruling: crashed OR restart-loop is the owned alarm ONLY with a proven restart loop of this exact unit since the onset (start_limit_eval: >= BURST-1 scheduled restarts, >= BURST-1 failed starts, then 'Start request repeated too quickly'; BURST is read from the unit). reset-failed gives each onset a fresh window. Duty ack owner/next/deadline, director routing, recovery and bounds are unchanged. Known diagnostic limit: on this host, systemd 258 keeps Result=exit-code after the start limit, so the frozen product reads crashed; no claim is made for all systemd versions.
corrections.L6: The deadline unit's exact callback argv is captured right after dispatch (l6_argv_eval: this binary, timer-callback, this qid, --action). The replay runs it as a process with AGENTDECK_PROFILE; l6_replay_eval requires rc 0, decision already-handled, and no new /cancel or director wake. An uncaptured argv is INCOMPLETE, never PASS.
corrections.stop_waits: L5 and L6b wait for run's own 'stop requested; exiting 64' journal line since the stop onset, plus the unit not active (stop_exited), instead of polling ExecMainStatus.
